content:
I recently noticed that Apple seems to have abandoned Cinematic Mode, and a video experiment perfectly demonstrates my disappointment with this.

It's not that the feature is bad, but that it's come so close to being truly usable that it's hard to understand why Apple hasn't made better use of the massive performance gains between the iPhone 13 that first introduced it and the latest iPhone. Let me show you…

I've previously explained that I understand why Apple hasn't made it a priority update, but I also believe they should — to encourage the next generation of video creators and filmmakers, especially teenagers who may not have access to other camera equipment.

I have a friend who uses a smartphone to interview strangers on the street and always manages to get them to open up about things you wouldn't imagine. I decided to turn the tables, put him on a stool, and film him the same way — this time with my iPhone 16 Pro Max.

I wanted to see how complex a scene Cinematic Mode could handle: a person sitting in the foreground, with railings about 25 feet behind him, and the O2 Arena nearly a thousand feet across the river. Add to that the fact that he'd be sitting on a stool, meaning very little movement.

The answer is… so close, yet so far. The overall effect isn't bad, but there's a noticeable halo between CK's legs and the railings, the O2's support pillars sometimes come into focus when he moves his head, and the river occasionally comes into focus when he stretches his arms out:

In CK's defence, he thinks the average viewer watching the footage wouldn't notice the problem. If they're not a filmmaker or a tech person familiar with how this feature works, they probably wouldn't notice these issues at all, or if they did, wouldn't find them bothersome. I suspect he may well be right.

But it really does bother me, and I think even amateur filmmaking enthusiasts would share my disappointment — and that's exactly the target audience for this feature.

As I said at the outset, my disappointment isn't because the feature is bad, but because I genuinely believe that if Apple fully leveraged the power of newer iPhone chips and their neural processing capabilities, this feature could be dramatically improved. In fact, I'd expect a better-updated version of Cinematic Mode to handle even more challenging environments than this.

Do you agree with my take? Do you want Apple to give Cinematic Mode a bit more love? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
